issue_context.title: DirectoryInfo.MoveTo() throws exception in cases where the directory initially did not exist but was created in the meantime
issue_context.body:
Edited (for original see below):

### Description
`DirectoryInfo.MoveTo` incorrectly checks for a file-existence in case its `Exist` property is `false` instead of checking for directory-existence.

To reproduce the exception run this code: (Works on .net4.x but fails on .netCore3.1 and onwards)

```csharp
using System;
using System.IO;

namespace N
{
	public class C
	{
		public static void Main()
		{
			string root = @"D:\";
			string originalPath = Path.Join(root, "52293_original");
			string movedPath = Path.Join(root, "52293_moved");

			if (Directory.Exists(originalPath))
			{
				Console.WriteLine("Original existed. Deleting.");
				Directory.Delete(originalPath, recursive: true);
			}

			if (Directory.Exists(movedPath))
			{
				Console.WriteLine("Moved existed. Deleting.");
				Directory.Delete(movedPath, recursive: true);
			}

			var info = new DirectoryInfo(originalPath);
                       
			Console.WriteLine($"Creating original: {originalPath}");
                        // The .Exist is relevant because it forces the directory info to initialize
			Console.WriteLine("OriginalExists:" + info.Exists);
			Directory.CreateDirectory(originalPath);

                        // .Exist is false at this point -> attempt to move will fail
			Console.WriteLine("Attempting to move.");
			info.MoveTo(movedPath);

			Console.WriteLine($"Successfully moved: {movedPath}");
		}
	}
}
```


EDIT: (This was the original description - edited with the text above to reflect the discussion afterwards)
### Description

`DirectoryInfo.MoveTo` does not work on .net core 3.1 on Windows when the directory is created right before on the same `DirectoryInfo`.

I.e. this code fails on `MoveTo` when `<TargetFramework>netcoreapp3.1</TargetFramework>`:

(Both directories need to be non-existent)

```csharp
using System;
using System.Diagnostics;
using System.IO;

namespace TestDirCreateCore
{
	class Program
	{
		static void Main(string[] args)
		{
			DirectoryInfo tempDirectoryInfo = new DirectoryInfo("t:\\testdir");

			Debug.WriteLine(tempDirectoryInfo.Exists);
			tempDirectoryInfo.Create();
			Debug.WriteLine(tempDirectoryInfo.Exists);
			tempDirectoryInfo.MoveTo("t:\\testdir2");
		}
	}
}
```

with the exception:

`System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException: 'Could not find a part of the path 't:\testdir'.'`

The same code works on .net4.7.2 and on .net5.0.

Note that on .net5.0 the second `tempDirectoryInfo.Exists` returns `true` while on .net4.7.2. it returns `false`.

Workaround: If `.Refresh()` is called before the `MoveTo()` the `Exists` property will return `true` and the move will no longer fail.

Uups, accidentally closed that by merging a PR on my own fork.

With the last code I can confirm there is an exception on `info.MoveTo(movedPath);` with latest public .Net 6.0 6.0.100-preview.3.21202.5  (but code in OP works well - please update repro steps to make it simple and clear! Please use latest .Net 6.0 Preview to prepare new fix and add tests in your PR).
@iSazonov What do you mean with "please update repro steps"? To edit the first comment on the issue?

> @iSazonov What do you mean with "please update repro steps"? To edit the first comment on the issue?

Yes, now this is more misleading than showing the problem.

> > @iSazonov What do you mean with "please update repro steps"? To edit the first comment on the issue?
> 
> Yes, now this is more misleading than showing the problem.

Ok, I changed the title and the initial description to match what was discovered during the investigation of this issue.

> Why didn't you use the example code I provided?

@ChristophHornung  I _did_ use your example, I used the latest one you shared in [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/52293#issuecomment-832836520), in which you said it was failing in .NET 3.1 and 5.0. You said:

> I think the underlying issue is still present even in .net5.

And

> This code works on .net4.7.2 but fails on both core3.1 and net5

The only things I did was replace the `Debug.WriteLine`s with `Console.WriteLine`s, and added the delete folder logic at the beginning.

Your proposed change in the linked PR is a breaking change on several tests, on all operating systems that we do not want to introduce. This can be confirmed by [the CI results](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/52310/checks?check_run_id=2511804469), in which several FileSystem tests are failing.

Adding an `Exists`/`Refresh`, is what the user is expected to do right before moving the filesystem object, and even then, there's no guarantee that we are going to be able to move the file/folder to a new location, because there could be other processes modifying the filesystem.

You can see this issue has been reported in [other places](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47186245/fileinfo-moveto-does-not-update-fileinfo-exists), with similar answers: Call `Refresh`.

Our documentation for `FileInfo.Exists` mentions this behavior [in the Remarks](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.fileinfo.exists?view=net-5.0#remarks). I also noticed we do not have this same remark described in `DirectoryInfo.Exists`, and maybe it should be added. I created [an issue in dotnet-api-docs](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-api-docs/issues/6746) to track this request.

The updated title and description match the expected behavior, so I'm closing this.

review_comments:
It seems `Exists` updates the cache if needed:
```suggestion
            if (!Exists)
```

> Exists does not know if the directory 'really' exists on the file system. (See e.g. my test via a `Directory.CreateDirectory` in #52293)

In the issue you said "Note that on .net5.0 the second tempDirectoryInfo.Exists returns true" - Where is the truth? :-)

`Exists` is correct if you create the directory through the `DirectoryInfo` object (as in the first example given in #52293, at least on .net5). But it does not if the directory was created without using the `DirectoryInfo` instance (like in the example given above).

In my opinion the exception should only be thrown when the file system tells us that the directory does not exist and not depend solely on the possibly incorrect `Exist` property. This would guarantee that no exception is thrown in case the directory exists in the file system, this would also match how .net4 code worked and it seems this was also the original intention of the code and `FileExists` was used in error.

Thanks for clarify! It would be nice to cover the scenario by new test.
